text:
ana: Quick debrief — ran burst load test at 11:00 and p99 drifted from 180ms -> 720ms for a ~45s window, looks correlated with scale-up events and KV cold misses. Anyone digging into kernel choices + microbatch sizing?
sam: saw the same. p95 stayed ~220ms, p99 exploded. tail looks like a handful of requests hit cold KV + fallback kernel. :frowning: 
deepa: I pulled the profiler traces. upload in a sec. initial hypothesis: prober chose small sample and we routed some requests to an older kernel variant that has worse attention kernel for longer seqs.
kai: posting heatmap.
```
-- profiler heatmap (attached) --
seq_len bucket: 128/256/512 rows
kernel_variant A: expected latency low for 128, but big hop at 512
kernel_variant B: stable at high seq but higher base
KV cache hit-rate: 93% before burst, dropped to 62% during spike
autoscaler: scaleup started at t+6s, nodes ready at t+22s
```
matt: important bits: microbatch size tuned for throughput (batch=64) so single-request latency is buffered. during burst we had many small requests leading to more batching jitter + kv misses. combined with kernel mismatch -> tail.
nana: @deploy-bot can you confirm if any deploys/rollbacks happened during the window?
deploy-bot: no deploys in that timeframe. Canary rollout finished earlier at t-15m.
sam: I also saw a perf regression flag in the nightly test: a new kernel heuristic change that prefers variant A for shorter avg seq. looks like it changed the threshold rounding.
deepa: added profiling diff: when routing rule favors A, p99 for seq512 jumps x3. attaching snippet of routing rule: 
```json
{"kernel_selector":{"seq_thresholds":[200,400],"prefer_low_latency":true}}
```
kai: interesting — the prober sampling window is too small to see the shift in seq distribution during the spike. prober picked variant A because recent samples were 80% <200 tokens. when burst contains a higher tail fraction, requests get misrouted.
matt: also KV cold misses amplify this: requests that land on newly provisioned nodes have empty KV, causing extra fetches and kernel fallback. combining three factors: misrouted kernel + microbatch buffering + kv cold = p99 spike.
nana: actionable suggestions?
sam: 1) increase prober sample window during high variance periods (or use stratified sampling), 2) prewarm KV on newly added nodes before routing, 3) tighten kernel-selector hysteresis for seq thresholds.
deepa: added a quick experiment plan: toggle kernel_selector.prefer_low_latency=false for 30m on a canary pool, run targeted burst, measure p95/p99 and kv-hit.
kai: and microbatch change: reduce max batch wait from 15ms -> 6ms for latency-sensitive pools during detected bursts. tradeoff: throughput drop ~6-8% in sim.
matt: We should also add a fallback route: if KV miss rate > 20% and prober variance > X, route new requests to the stable kernel B until node warm-up.
nana: agree. can we get a short runbook for oncall to mitigate in-prod? p99 spikes woke a couple of customers.
deepa: I'll draft runbook: commands to prewarm: 
```bash
# prewarm kv on pool nodes
for node in $(list-new-nodes); do curl -s "http://node.internal/prewarm?model=${MODEL}&seq=256" & done
```
and toggles to flip kernel selector flag via config service.
sam: timeline: I can run the canary experiment at 16:30. need approvals from infra to prewarm.
kai: I'll update the prober logic PR with stratified sampling and larger window. will aim for a patch by EOD.
matt: I'll add metric alerts for KV hit-rate + kernel mismatch ratio so we can auto-detect this combo.
nana: thanks team. let's sync in eng-runtime standup tomorrow and publish the runbook link in #oncall. :thumbsup:
